livingStudio.name: Air BnB Living Studio
livingStudio.tagline: Not a showroom — a home we built ourselves.
livingStudio.body: A guesthouse we built ourselves — our own stone, flooring, finishes and furniture throughout. Stay the night, live with every surface and plan your project from inside a working home.

stays.name: The Living Studio
stays.blurb: Our flagship stayable showroom — every surface is our own work.
stays.description: The premium way to experience BDS Marvel: a full guesthouse built end-to-end with our own stone, flooring, finishes and furniture. Stay the night, host your architect over breakfast, walk the materials library with our consultant and specify your project from inside a working reference.

stays.name: The Stone Pavilion
stays.blurb: A pavilion of glass and our own basalt, wrapped around a reflecting pool.
stays.description: Four suites arranged around a still reflecting pool, every wall in basalt we cut ourselves. Evenings on the water court, mornings in the sauna — the full BDS Marvel material palette at its most resolved.

stays.name: The Marble House
stays.blurb: Lake-facing suites in book-matched marble, ten minutes from the old city.
stays.description: A lake-facing residence where every bathroom is book-matched marble from our Kishangarh workshop. Sunset terraces, a butler pantry and quiet, cool rooms that show what stone does to light.

stays.name: The Verandah Suite
stays.blurb: A shaded laterite verandah, a plunge pool and nothing to prove.
stays.description: Our Goan outpost: laterite walls, a deep shaded verandah and a plunge pool under the trees. Two suites, an outdoor kitchen and the quietest version of our material palette.

stays.name: The BDS Penthouse
stays.blurb: Our city showcase — a split-level penthouse over the sea link skyline.
stays.description: The city flagship: a split-level penthouse with a double-height stone wall, terrazzo stair and a screening lounge. Host your project team, walk the flat with our designers and leave with a spec sheet.

stays.name: The Material Loft
stays.blurb: A warm city loft finished in our stone and oak — design comfort without the ceremony.
stays.description: A two-bedroom city loft for travellers who want to live with good material without the full showroom programme. Oak plank floors, honed stone counters and hand-finished lime walls — the same spec we install for clients, at an easy nightly rate.

stays.name: The Oak Apartment
stays.blurb: Wall-to-wall oak, soft light and a proper work table.
stays.description: A calm two-bedroom apartment panelled in our engineered oak, with a long work table for travelling teams and a kitchen that invites slow mornings.

stays.name: The Kota Flat
stays.blurb: A sunlit one-bed on Kota stone floors, minutes from the metro.
stays.description: A bright one-bedroom flat that shows off what humble Kota stone can do — cool floors, warm textiles, a reading corner and an easy commute to anywhere in the city.

stays.name: The Terrace Rooms
stays.blurb: Two rooms, one big planted terrace, evening breeze included.
stays.description: A two-bedroom stay built around its planted terrace — outdoor dining for six, warm wood interiors and blackout shutters for proper sleep after long site days.

stays.name: The Weaver's Stay
stays.blurb: Textiles, lime plaster and a courtyard cafe downstairs.
stays.description: A one-bedroom stay above a courtyard cafe in the old textile district — lime plaster walls, handloom throws and our stone in the bath. Quiet, central, easy.

stays.name: The Courtyard Room
stays.blurb: A simple, honest room beside our workshop — stone underfoot, sun in the courtyard.
stays.description: Our budget-friendly stay: a quiet, light-filled room next to the Kishangarh workshop. Honest materials, a proper bed, a shaded courtyard and chai from the studio kitchen. Perfect for a night between site visits — or your first look at what we make.

stays.name: The Studio Nook
stays.blurb: A neat little room five minutes from the dargah road.
stays.description: The simplest stay we make: a crisp bed, a writing desk, a hot shower and morning sun. Everything you need between trains, site visits and long drives.

stays.name: The Workshop Room
stays.blurb: Fall asleep to the smell of cut stone — a room inside our workshop compound.
stays.description: A snug room inside the workshop compound for people who want to wake up where the material is made. Early morning cutting demos if you ask nicely.

stays.name: The Sunroom
stays.blurb: A glass-cornered room that catches the desert morning.
stays.description: A corner room wrapped in glass on two sides, five minutes from the lake ghats. Sunrise does the decorating; we did the stone floor and the very good mattress.

stays.name: The Lime Wash Room
stays.blurb: Hand-trowelled lime walls and a deep, dark night's sleep.
stays.description: A cocoon of hand-trowelled lime plaster in the old city — cool in summer, warm at night, with a tiny balcony for evening chai. Our cheapest night, and many guests' favourite.

stayTiers.name: Premium
stayTiers.headline: Experience our work, first-hand.
stayTiers.copy: Full homes built end-to-end with our own stone, floors and furniture — hosted walkthroughs, chef breakfasts and the materials library. Live in the reference before you specify it.

stayTiers.name: Mid
stayTiers.headline: Design comfort, city ease.
stayTiers.copy: Finished apartments wearing our oak, stone and lime — work tables, good kitchens, self check-in and easy nightly rates.

stayTiers.name: Budget-friendly
stayTiers.headline: Honest rooms, honest prices.
stayTiers.copy: Simple, light-filled rooms near our workshops and the old cities — the essentials done properly, from ₹3,900 a night.

approach.title: MATERIAL FIRST
approach.text: Every project begins with the stone or the surface. Specification precedes drawings so the material never has to bend to fit the design.

approach.title: ONE TEAM
approach.text: Materials, flooring, construction and interiors under one roof. One accountable team from the spec sheet to the snag list.

approach.title: EDITORIAL DETAIL
approach.text: Architectural minimalism, hospitality warmth. Joints, thresholds and reveals resolved with the same care as the elevation.

approach.title: HERITAGE + CRAFT
approach.text: Traditional cutting and finishing techniques paired with modern engineering. Craftspeople we have worked with for two decades.

approach.title: EXPERIENCE-LED
approach.text: Don't just see the materials — live in them. The BDSM Living Studio is our showroom you can actually stay in.

projects.title: Meridian Residences
projects.description: Twelve seafront villas clad in a custom facade stone quarried, cut and installed end-to-end.
projects.challenge: The facade needed to weather the salt air without turning grey.
projects.approach: We specified a dense sandstone with a low porosity and honed it to bring the warm undertones forward.

projects.title: Kabbon Lounge
projects.description: A 90-cover restaurant designed around a single travertine bar block.
projects.challenge: The client wanted the room to feel monolithic without becoming cold.
projects.approach: One stone, three finishes — a polished bar top, honed cladding, split-face walls. Warm oak floors soften everything else.

projects.title: Veda Clubhouse
projects.description: A residential clubhouse — pool, gym, event spaces — built as one continuous stone ribbon.
projects.challenge: Every wall inside and out had to read as the same material.
projects.approach: We wrapped the volume in a Kota-limestone rain screen and continued the same stone through the pool coping and lobby floor.

projects.title: Annex Workspace
projects.description: 40,000 sqft of workspace flooring across three floors, delivered in a six-week window.
projects.challenge: A hospitality-grade floor that could take a corporate footfall.
projects.approach: Contract-grade SPC in two warm tones, pre-cut off-site so installation ran cleanly.

projects.title: Atrium Mall
projects.description: Retail atrium with a book-matched onyx feature wall and a full-marble concourse.
projects.challenge: Matching stone across 45 running metres of feature wall.
projects.approach: We sourced two adjacent onyx blocks, cut them ourselves, and book-matched every panel before shipping.

projects.title: Shore Villa
projects.description: A four-bedroom villa where every fixed surface is stone.
projects.challenge: Keep a heavy-material palette from feeling like a museum.
projects.approach: Three warm marbles, natural lime plaster, oak floors and light linen textiles. Nothing else.

projects.title: Civic Facade
projects.description: A civic building facade in flame-finished granite installed as a dry-cladding system.
projects.challenge: A facade that would read cleanly at scale and stay clean over the years.
projects.approach: Self-cleaning flame finish, a 4mm shadow gap and a sub-frame built to hold thermal movement.

projects.title: Kiln Restaurant
projects.description: A 3,200 sqft restaurant built around an exposed brick and stone kiln.
projects.challenge: Structural rework to expose the kiln without losing the load path.
projects.approach: We ran a new steel transfer above the kiln and let the original masonry become the room.

projects.title: Lumen Apartment
projects.description: A full interior-designing brief for a light-first city apartment, resolved end-to-end before a single wall moved.
projects.challenge: A dark, compartmentalised flat that needed to feel open without losing storage.
projects.approach: We redrew the plan around a single daylight axis, set a warm neutral palette and detailed every joinery run in 3D before build.

projects.title: Sable Studio Office
projects.description: Interior designing for a creative studio — spatial planning, material palette and lighting concept delivered as one scheme.
projects.challenge: Give a 20-person studio focus zones and social zones inside one open floor.
projects.approach: Zoning by material and light: honed stone at the core, warm oak at the edges, layered task and ambient lighting throughout.

principles.title: Material comes first
principles.text: Before the drawing, we specify the stone or the surface. The rest of the project is designed around what the material actually wants to do.

principles.title: One accountable team
principles.text: Materials, flooring, construction and interiors all report into a single project lead. Fewer handovers, fewer things lost in translation.

principles.title: Detail is a discipline
principles.text: Every joint, threshold and reveal is drawn before it's built. Nothing is decided on site that could have been decided at the desk.

principles.title: Craft is not decorative
principles.text: Traditional cutting and finishing techniques are part of the engineering — not a nostalgia bolted on at the end.

principles.title: Experience over pitch
principles.text: Instead of a moodboard, we invite clients to stay in a space that uses our full palette. Specify from inside the reference.

principles.title: Long horizons
principles.text: We build for how a space looks in year ten, not the day it opens.
